diagnostic_steps.action: Parse log stream for image pull errors
findings: DNS resolution error: 'no such host' for registry.azurecr.io
Connection refused and TLS handshake timeout errors
All 3 order-processor pods in ImagePullBackOff state
External DNS resolution failing for ACR domain
Network unreachable from worker nodes to ACR
ACR registry.azurecr.io is accessible from outside cluster
ACR integration with AKS may be misconfigured
No custom DNS server configured for ACR resolution
Root cause: DNS resolution failure for ACR domain
Contributing factor: ACR DNS not resolving from cluster nodes
Possible cause: Azure Private Link or VNet DNS misconfiguration
Alternative cause: ACR firewall blocking cluster IP range
diagnostic_steps.root_cause: DNS resolution failure for Azure Container Registry from cluster

recommendations.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: azure-resolver
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  Corefile: |
    azurecr.io:53 {
        errors
        cache 30
        forward 168.63.129.16  # Azure DNS
    }
EOF
recommendations.rationale: Add Azure DNS forwarder for ACR domain resolution
Update CoreDNS to forward ACR queries to Azure DNS

recommendations.command: kubectl rollout restart deployment coredns -n kube-system
recommendations.rationale: Restart CoreDNS to apply new configuration
Re-attach ACR to AKS to refresh authentication and DNS

recommendations.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-registry-egress
  namespace: order-service
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
EOF
recommendations.rationale: Ensure network policy allows egress to ACR
Ensure image pull secret is properly configured
